weight lifting > diet > cardio

research information and plan a main goal and sub goals (they don't have to be super specific or anything)

each exercise you do, write down what you accomplished so you know NEXT TIME what you need to do OR better (so you will need a log, either electronic or paper and that should be specific. example: day 1 - 1 mile, day 2 - 1.2 miles, etc)

You don't need to know your weight so you don't need a scale. Your accomplishment log is more important. If you do weight yourself you might find that your weight goes up initially before going down. This happened to me and a friend in the first 4-6 weeks. don't worry about that, just keep with the plan. You may notice loss about the 7th week.

get a heart rate monitor or just calculate it and keep it in the zone for cardio, not too hard, not too slow

get rid of any food/drinks containing (as much as you can) High fructose corn syrup and soybean oil. you may need vitamins as well.

ALWAYS stretch before exercising and after. take at least 1 day off a week and just do stretches or relax.
REST between exercising - Your body needs time to recover. You can alternate exercises/muscle groups to work on so you don't do the same thing every day and the previous group has rest time. So like, day 1 arms, day 2 cardio, day 3 legs, 4 more cardio, 5 shoulders/back, 6 cardio, 7 rest/stretch only. see now your arms have had 6 rest days but you still exercised near the whole week.
